skill.name: frontend-security-coder
skill.description: Guides secure frontend coding for XSS prevention, safe DOM handling, CSP, input validation, secure redirects, and browser security features.
skill.summary: Guides secure frontend implementation for XSS prevention, CSP, validation, redirects, and browser protections.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive: SKILL.md line 26 uses Markdown backticks to format a resource path, not shell execution. I found no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or other semantic security abuse in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged backticks are Markdown inline code around a documentation path, not Ruby or shell execution. SKILL.md contains prose instructions only and no executable command invocation at that location.

content.value_statement: Frontend teams often miss client-side flaws that lead to XSS, unsafe redirects, and weak browser protections. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to implement secure UI patterns and focused frontend security reviews.
actual_capabilities: Recommends safe DOM APIs such as textContent and secure element creation.
Guides XSS prevention with sanitization, encoding, and secure templating practices.
Helps configure CSP directives, nonces, hashes, and violation reporting.
Reviews redirects, URL handling, third-party widgets, and iframe sandboxing.
Provides frontend security checklists for authentication, sessions, PWAs, and browser headers.
limitations: Does not include executable scanners or automated vulnerability testing.
Cannot prove server-side security without backend code and deployment context.
Referenced implementation playbook is not present in the scanned package.
Client-side guidance still requires testing in target browsers and frameworks.

use_cases.title: Harden User Content Rendering
use_cases.description: Implement safer rendering for comments, markdown, rich text, and dynamic UI updates.

use_cases.title: Review Client-Side Controls
use_cases.description: Check existing UI code for XSS, redirect, CSP, token storage, and iframe risks.

use_cases.title: Secure Third-Party Integrations
use_cases.description: Plan safer analytics, payment, chat, and widget integrations with SRI, sandboxing, and privacy limits.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component for XSS
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend component for XSS risks. Focus on DOM APIs, template output, and user-supplied data. Suggest minimal fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Safe Input Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add client-side validation for this form. Use allowlists, safe URL handling, and clear error states. Keep backend validation assumptions explicit.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CSP Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased CSP plan for this frontend app. Include report-only mode, nonce or hash strategy, third-party scripts, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Complex Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this third-party widget integration. Address iframe sandboxing, postMessage validation, SRI, privacy constraints, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: A user profile page renders names, bios, and uploaded rich text.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review that separates trusted and untrusted content, recommends safer rendering APIs, and identifies where sanitization is required.

output_examples.input: A team wants to deploy CSP without breaking analytics and payments.
output_examples.output: A phased rollout plan with report-only testing, nonce or hash guidance, third-party source review, and violation monitoring steps.

output_examples.input: A redirect parameter sends users to a destination after login.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to replace open URL parameters with fixed destination identifiers, allowlist checks, and clear fallback behavior.

best_practices: Provide the threat model, framework, browser targets, and trusted content sources.
Ask for minimal patches that preserve current user flows and accessibility.
Validate recommendations with tests, browser behavior, and security headers in deployment.
anti_patterns: Relying on client-side validation as the only security control.
Requesting generic security advice without code, context, or accepted tradeoffs.
Adding broad CSP exceptions such as unsafe-inline before testing safer options.

faq.question: Can this skill write secure frontend code?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides implementation guidance for safer DOM handling, CSP, validation, redirects, and browser security features.

faq.question: Does it replace a full security audit?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on frontend implementation and review, not penetration testing or compliance sign-off.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with React or Vue?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide component code and framework constraints. It can adapt guidance to common frontend patterns.

faq.question: Does it run external scanners?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prompt guidance only and does not include executable scanner code.

faq.question: How should I verify its recommendations?
faq.answer: Use unit tests, browser tests, CSP reports, dependency checks, and application security review for risky flows.
